Q1: The failing test can't be identified from the evidence. What should this issue do?
Choices:
A) Make CI failures easier to diagnose. When a shard fails, have the orchestrate-poll sharding step repeat the failed shard's `FAIL` test names and its last error lines in the final `::error::` summary, so log tails and future triages show what failed. Add a matching assertion in `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`. Don't touch poller behavior or the PR #6940 renderer, and don't loosen how failures are counted. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Do the same as A, and also apply it to the identical sharded step in the release gates' `validate-scripts` job (`mark-stable.yml`, `test-and-mark-stable.yml`). The sharding contract test already requires these copies to match.
C) Change no code. Close the issue as inconclusive or possibly flaky, and rerun the failed `orchestrate-poll (3)` job on PR #6940 instead.
D) Hold the issue until an operator adds the failing test name from the full log of run 37935250730 (at check-run head `795be54a…`). Then fix that specific test or poller behavior.
**Note:** C and D don't fit the unattended pipeline well. D needs a human to pull the log, and C produces no PR.
